title: MCP Enterprise Features (2026)
content:
## Overview

Through 2026, the Model Context Protocol has matured from an open-source developer standard into an enterprise-grade infrastructure layer. Key milestones include the MCP 2.4 specification, governance transfer to the Linux Foundation, Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) with Okta SSO, and MCP Tunnels for private-network access.

---

## MCP 2.4 Specification

The MCP 2.4 spec (2026) added three enterprise governance features:

- **Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for high-risk tool calls** — servers can tag individual tools as requiring step-up auth before execution
- **Real-time audit logs** — all tool invocations are streamed to the MCP Admin Console, giving compliance teams a complete record of what agents did and when
- **Improved consent workflows** — users can grant scoped, time-limited permissions rather than blanket tool access

These additions address the key gap between developer prototypes and production enterprise deployments.

---

## Linux Foundation Governance

In December 2025, Anthropic transferred stewardship of MCP to the **Linux Foundation**. This positions MCP alongside other neutral open standards (OpenTelemetry, Kubernetes, Envoy) rather than as a proprietary Anthropic protocol. Major vendors including Salesforce Agentforce, Cloudflare, Replit, and Microsoft Azure OpenAI have since added native MCP support.

As of mid-2026, the official MCP server registry lists **over 9,400 servers**.

---

## Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA)

Anthropic launched EMA on June 18, 2026. The feature replaces per-user OAuth consent screens with a zero-touch, identity-provider-delegated flow.

### How it works

1. An enterprise IT admin configures MCP connector access once through their identity provider (IdP)
2. On first login, employees automatically receive access to the configured connectors — no per-user OAuth prompt required
3. Access is centrally managed: revoking a user in the IdP immediately revokes their MCP connector access

**Okta** is the first supported IdP at launch; VS Code Copilot and Claude Code are among the first supported clients.

### Initial connector support

Seven MCP providers support EMA at launch:

| Provider | Category |
|----------|----------|
| Asana | Project management |
| Atlassian | Dev tools (Jira, Confluence) |
| Canva | Design |
| Figma | Design |
| Granola | Meeting notes |
| Linear | Issue tracking |
| Supabase | Database / backend |

---

## MCP Tunnels

Anthropic introduced **MCP Tunnels** (research preview) to solve a long-standing friction point: enterprise MCP servers often run on internal networks and can't be reached by cloud-hosted agents without exposing them to the public internet.

### What tunnels enable

- Claude Managed Agents and the Messages API can connect to private MCP servers behind corporate firewalls
- No public IP or firewall rule changes required on the server side
- The tunnel authenticates at the Anthropic layer; internal servers only need to trust the tunnel endpoint
- Organizations can expose internal databases, code repositories, and ITSM tools to AI agents without adding public-facing attack surface

MCP Tunnels are available in **research preview** via the Claude Developer Platform. Self-hosted sandboxes for Claude Managed Agents were released alongside tunnels, providing isolated execution environments for agent-run code.

---

## Claude Managed Agents API

Alongside these infrastructure improvements, Anthropic's **Managed Agents API** now supports connecting MCP servers directly to cloud-hosted agents. This means developers can define an agent with a set of MCP servers and deploy it without managing agent infrastructure themselves — Anthropic handles routing, retries, and observability.

---

## Ecosystem Scale

| Metric | Value (mid-2026) |
|--------|------------------|
| Official MCP server registry | 9,400+ servers |
| Enterprise platforms with native MCP | Salesforce, Cloudflare, Replit, Azure OpenAI, and others |
| Governance body | Linux Foundation (since Dec 2025) |
| EMA launch IdP | Okta |
| EMA launch connectors | 7 providers |

The combination of Linux Foundation stewardship, a growing registry, and enterprise auth/tunneling features positions MCP as a durable protocol for AI-to-tool connectivity rather than a transient framework.
